Defined by gastrointestinal stromal tumors, pulmonary chondromas and endocrine paragangliomas.
Disorder of lipid metabolism; atherosclerotic disease is a separate downstream disease.
Oxalate metabolic disorder defined by renal crystal deposition and injury. Hepatic enzyme deficiency does not imply liver damage; anemia alone does not establish direct marrow injury.
Defective glycinergic neurotransmission causes exaggerated startle and hypertonia; stiffness and episodic apnea do not establish intrinsic muscle or pulmonary injury.
Isolated inherited cataract affecting the lens.
Intraepithelial neoplasia arising in the conjunctiva.
Central and peripheral neurodegeneration defines SPG11. Retinal degeneration and visual impairment are occasional; dysphagia and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Adipocytic neoplasms commonly arise in subcutaneous fat, covered by dermatologic; deep locations vary and do not establish another shared organ axis.
Congenital duplication of the pyloric portion of the stomach.
Isolated dystonia affects motor control; laryngeal and oromandibular dystonia do not establish intrinsic airway or oral tissue damage.
Intellectual disability and eyelid abnormalities define the syndrome. Musculoskeletal involvement includes clubfoot in 50%, joint hypermobility in 60% and cervical fusion in 30%.
Inherited abnormal radiosensitivity of natural killer activity is an immune functional phenotype; no other organ damage is documented.
Arthrogryposis, myopathy and scoliosis define it. Cleft palate, conductive hearing impairment and ptosis each occur in 30-79%; evidence comes from very few families.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, regression and cerebral abnormalities.
Familial hidradenitis suppurativa is an immune-mediated inflammatory follicular skin disease causing abscesses and scarring.
Epiphyseal skeletal dysplasia causing osteochondral abnormalities and early joint degeneration across the group.
Congenital orofacial cleft affecting lip or palate; oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Autoantibodies damage the neuromuscular junction. Muscle weakness and ocular or bulbar symptoms arise from impaired neuromuscular transmission.
Lipomatous neural tube defect directly tethers spinal cord and roots. Sphincter dysfunction is neurogenic; direct urinary or bowel injury and qualifying skeletal frequency are unestablished.
X-linked intellectual developmental disorder; seizures also affect the neurologic axis. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal injury.
Chordoma arises from notochordal remnants in the axial skeleton; proximity to the CNS does not establish neurologic involvement.
Narcolepsy type 1 involves loss of hypothalamic hypocretin neurons, generally through an immune-mediated process. Autonomic symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Selective loss of smell perception; smell is explicitly assigned to the neurologic axis.

Complex I metabolic deficiency; leukodystrophy and developmental impairment are core. Neurologic disease and myopathy with ragged-red fibers occur in 1/1 annotated patient; frequency evidence is limited.
